key_insight: Distilling a fixed atomistic foundation model into compact potentials preserves key semiconductor-interface thermal and mechanical responses while enabling simulations several orders of magnitude faster and larger.
engineering_relevance: Compact distilled potentials offer a practical route to large-scale interface simulations for thermal management and mechanical reliability studies.
method: Select an EquiformerV3 teacher from 128 pretrained models across 22 families.
Train ACE and NEP students without target-specific teacher fine-tuning.
Compare distilled and DFT-trained students using matched training configurations and architectures.
evidence_signal: For 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces, thermal conductance differed by at most 6.6% from DFT-trained counterparts; for 29,792-atom Cu/diamond specimens at 500 K, tensile strength and loading work differed by 2.8% and 1.5%, respectively.
watch_item: Committee-based selection improved high-error force fitting but did not consistently improve downstream properties, so interface-level validation remains important.
paper_title: Distilling an atomistic foundation model is all you need for large-scale molecular dynamics of semiconductor interfaces
